- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) mid-period, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33) — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days in capturing sentiment-driven momentum — adjust forecast to align with sentiment peak 1–2 days ahead.
- If sentiment shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.67), model may overfit recent data; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
